a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines the proposition asserting that for every set K of arithmetic sentences (closed formulas in the language of first-order arithmetic) and every arithmetic theory F (a set of arithmetic sentences, not necessarily closed under deduction), assuming that (1) F is recursively enumerable, (2) every theorem of IΣ₁ (basic arithmetic with induction for Σ₁ formulas) is a theorem of F, (3) K equals F.theory (the set of all sentences derivable from F in classical first-order logic), and (4) K is consistent as an arithmetic theory (it does not prove a contradiction), it follows that the consistency sentence F.craig.consistent.val is not an element of K — where F.craig.consistent.val is the arithmetic sentence ¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝) formed using the standard provability predicate built from F.craig, the Δ₁-presented axiom set with the same theorems as F obtained by Craig's trick. No soundness (truth in the standard model ℕ) is required, and no Δ₁ presentation of F itself is assumed beyond F being recursively enumerable."}

divergences.description: Conclusion formalizes unprovability of consistency (Def7 F ∉ K) rather than unknowability of soundness (Penrose's 'knowably sound algorithm' and Koellner's K(F ⊆ T) → F ⊊ K in [P-K356]). Truth/soundness of F (F ⊆ T) cannot be expressed as a single sentence in ℒₒᵣ, so the formalization does not state soundness-knowledge or the bridge principle that knowing soundness entails knowing consistency (though under that informal bridge, failing to prove consistency is the stronger negative conclusion). Moreover, contraposing Target only yields K ≠ F.theory, not Koellner's strict containment F ⊊ K.

The hypothesis assumes only consistency (Def4 K) rather than soundness (Def3 K), whereas Chalmers [P-C1] ('if our reasoning powers are capturable by some sound formal system F') and Penrose [P-K356] assume soundness. Because soundness implies consistency, this is a harmless strengthening of the theorem (matching Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem in [P-K345] and the author's own phrasing).

Target adds the explicit strength hypothesis [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F] and restricts both K and F to sets of sentences in first-order arithmetic (ℒₒᵣ) closed under classical first-order deduction (F.theory). This concretizes [P-K345]'s 'sufficiently strong formal system' and leaves implicit the strength requirement in [P-C1], while narrowing the claim from general mathematical reasoning, algorithms, or non-arithmetical / non-classical formal systems.

Def7 F is defined as F.craig.consistent.val, the standard consistency sentence for the specific Δ₁-presented axiom set obtained from F via Craig's trick rather than for F's own presentation. Thus Target only rules out membership in K of that particular Craig-trick consistency sentence, rather than quantifying over natural Δ₁ presentations of F or addressing the intensionality of consistency statements.

The mind and its epistemic capacities ('ascertain', 'see that F is consistent', 'determine', K(·)) are idealized extensionally as a bare set of arithmetic sentences K with σ ∈ K standing for establishing σ; once K = F.theory is substituted, K drops out and Target reduces directly to Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem for F. In addition, Target only rules out proving Con(F.craig), not refuting it (as in Koellner's 'prove or refute' in [P-K356]), since a merely consistent K = F.theory can consistently contain ∼Con(F.craig).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the core conditional conclusion—matching Chalmers [P-C1] and Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem [P-K345]—that if a consistent mind K coincides with the theorems of a sufficiently strong RE arithmetic theory F, then K cannot contain F's consistency sentence. Its divergences are minor formalization caveats: it uses consistency rather than soundness as the hypothesis, leaves Penrose's 'knowably sound' and Koellner's truth-based K(F ⊆ T) → F ⊊ K unformalized in favor of Con(F.craig), restricts to classical first-order arithmetic extending 𝗜𝚺₁, and models epistemic establishment extensionally via set membership.
